statement: Show an infinite sequence \(a_1, a_2, \ldots\) of integers with both of the following properties: (i) \(a_i \neq 0\) for every positive integer \(i\); (ii) for all positive integers \(n\), \(a_n + a_{2n} + \cdots + a_{2023n} = 0\).

Let \(ABC\) be a right triangle with the right angle at \(B\), with altitude \(BT\) where \(T\) is on the hypotenuse \(AC\). Construct equilateral triangles \(BTX\) and \(BTY\) so that \(X\) is in the same half-plane as \(A\) with respect to \(BT\), and \(Y\) is in the same half-plane as \(C\) with respect to \(BT\). Let \(P\) be the intersection of lines \(AY\) and \(CX\). Show that \[PA \cdot BC = PB \cdot CA = PC \cdot AB.\]

Let \(n\) be a positive integer. The SpaceY and SpaceZ agencies travel alternately between Earth and Mars, with SpaceY making the first trip. On each trip, the responsible agency does one of two types of mission:

i) Choose a positive integer \(k\) and take \(k\) people to Mars, creating a new colony and settling them in it;

ii) Choose some existing colony on Mars and a positive integer \(k\) strictly smaller than the population of that colony, and bring \(k\) people from that colony back to Earth.

A mission cannot result in two colonies with the same population, and the number of colonies must be at most \(n\). The first agency that cannot carry out a mission will go bankrupt. Determine, in terms of \(n\), which agency can guarantee that it will not go bankrupt first.
Let \(x, y, z\) be three distinct real numbers such that \(x^2 - x = yz\), \(y^2 - y = zx\), \(z^2 - z = xy\). Show that \(-\dfrac{1}{3} < x, y, z < 1\).

Let \(m\) be a positive integer with \(m \leq 2024\). Ana and Banana play a game alternately on a \(1 \times 2024\) board, with squares initially painted white. Ana starts the game. Each move by Ana consists of choosing any \(k \leq m\) white squares on the board and painting them all green. Each move by Banana consists of choosing any sequence of consecutive green squares and painting them all white. What is the smallest value of \(m\) for which Ana can guarantee that, after one of her moves, the entire board will be painted green?

For a positive integer \(k\), let \(p(k)\) be the smallest prime that does not divide \(k\). Given a positive integer \(a\), define the infinite sequence \(a_0, a_1, \ldots\) by \(a_0 = a\) and, for \(n > 0\), \(a_n\) is the smallest positive integer different from \(a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}\) such that \((a_{n-1})^{a_n} - 1\) is a multiple of \(p(a_{n-1})\). Prove that every positive integer appears in the sequence.
